Forcesteed develops AI-assisted robot programming with human approval

Luqua combines taught motions, rule-based control and VLA skills within FOS, with product development continuing.

Forcesteed Robotics / PR TIMES ↗29 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 6

Turning requests into steps

Forcesteed has developed Agentic Robotics within FOS. Its local Luqua agent decomposes a requested job into stages such as finding, approaching, grasping, placing and checking, then assembles a node program through LEIVOR. Local operation targets sites without reliable internet access.

Combining control methods

Individual stages can use rule-based vision and planning, a learned VLA model or manually taught motion. An operator identifies a failed stage and the agent proposes a targeted revision. Approved motions, skills and tasks become reusable assets to reduce repeated programming.

Approval before execution

People review, edit or approve programs and define exclusion zones and stop conditions. The agent reasons before execution and after failures, while existing controllers execute motions. Internal and partner trials precede productization; simulation success does not establish real-machine safety.
